name: Tether
desc: Issues USDT, the largest US-dollar stablecoin, and invests profits in bitcoin, AI and media companies.
capacity_detail: Valued at about USD 350bn (Feb 2026), per the unicorn list and cited Forbes article
markets: Worldwide USDT users outside the United States; planned US-domiciled stablecoin USAT; El Salvador base
rationale: Crypto exchanges and stablecoin rivals such as Circle, Coinbase and OKX already use F1 to build trust and global awareness.

name: DJI
desc: Makes consumer and professional drones, handheld gimbal cameras and action cameras sold in markets worldwide.
markets: China, Japan, North America, Europe and Latin America divisions; over 90% of the global consumer drone market
rationale: Global camera and drone brand selling to filmmakers and enthusiasts; F1 broadcast and content production showcase aerial and onboard imaging.

name: Mistral AI
desc: Develops open-weight and commercial large language models and the Vibe assistant for businesses and consumers.
capacity_detail: Raised EUR 2bn at a EUR 12bn (about USD 14bn) valuation in Sep 2025
markets: European enterprises and governments, with partners including Microsoft, NVIDIA and Accenture; datacenters in France and Sweden

signals.raise: Samsung took a stake in a EUR 3bn transaction (Sep 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_AI)

rationale: European AI champion competing with Anthropic, Google and Microsoft, all F1 partners; F1 offers global B2B visibility.

name: Ola Consumer
desc: Indian ride-hailing app (formerly Ola Cabs) operated by ANI Technologies, offering cabs, autos and bikes.
markets: More than 250 Indian cities; exited the UK, Australia and New Zealand in April 2024
rationale: Mass-market Indian mobility brand; F1's fast-growing Indian audience could support brand building, though spending is domestic.

name: Tenstorrent
desc: Designs RISC-V CPUs and AI inference accelerator chips, led by chip architect Jim Keller.
capacity_detail: Raised USD 1.5bn at a USD 6.2bn valuation (Oct 2026)
markets: Offices across the US, Canada, India, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and Europe serving AI and chip customers
rationale: AI chip challenger to NVIDIA and AMD; AMD, Arm and Groq already use F1 for engineering-led B2B branding.

name: Toss (Viva Republica)
desc: Runs Toss, a South Korean financial super-app for payments, transfers, banking, investing and insurance.
markets: South Korea, with over 20 million users, and Vietnam
rationale: Leading Korean fintech brand; rivals such as Revolut and Nu use F1 for consumer reach and international expansion.

name: CloudKitchens
desc: Leases delivery-only commercial kitchens to restaurants and food brands, led by Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick.
markets: United States, United Kingdom, Mexico, Colombia, Brazil and the Middle East
rationale: B2B real-estate operator with little consumer brand; F1 hospitality could reach restaurant partners but fit is weak.

name: Sorare
desc: Fantasy sports game with licensed digital player cards for football, basketball and baseball.
capacity_detail: Series B USD 680M (Sep 2021) at a USD 4.3bn valuation
sponsorships: Licensing partnerships: La Liga (2021), MLB (2022), NBA (2022), Premier League (2023)
markets: Football, basketball and baseball fans worldwide on web, iOS and Android; regulatory focus on France and UK
rationale: Sports-licensing business model fits F1; a licensed F1 driver-card game would extend its fantasy portfolio.

name: Abnormal AI
desc: Sells AI-based email and collaboration security software that stops phishing and account takeover attacks.
markets: Enterprises including more than 30% of the Fortune 500
rationale: Cybersecurity rivals CrowdStrike, Zscaler and 1Password use F1 for enterprise awareness and hospitality with CISOs.

name: Branch
desc: Provides mobile deep-linking and attribution software that helps apps track and route users across channels.
capacity_detail: Rounds of USD 3M, 15M, 35M, 60M (2014-2017) + Series F USD 300M (Feb 2022)
markets: App developers and brands; only the US headquarters is stated
rationale: B2B marketing technology firm; F1 hospitality could reach app marketers, but brand-led fit is limited.

name: Articulate
desc: Makes Articulate 360 and Rise e-learning authoring software used by organisations to build employee training courses.
capacity_detail: USD 1.5bn round led by General Atlantic (Jul 2021)
markets: 125,000 organisations in 187 countries, including all of the Fortune 100
rationale: Enterprise software brand selling globally; Udemy and Workday use F1 to court corporate buyers.

name: Kurly
desc: Runs Market Kurly, a South Korean online grocery and beauty retailer with overnight cold-chain delivery.
capacity_detail: Consolidated revenue KRW 2.3671 trillion (about USD 1.7bn) in 2025
markets: South Korea only, with logistics centres in Gimpo, Pyeongtaek and Changwon

signals.raise: Naver joined a capital increase (Jul 2026; https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/컬리_(기업))

rationale: Domestic consumer brand; F1 would mainly serve Korean awareness and premium positioning, so fit is limited.
